key_insight: Diffusion-based reconstruction can detect fatal cerebral hemorrhage on postmortem CT, and weak image-level supervision performs best.
clinical_relevance: This could help automate triage of forensic brain CT scans by flagging cases that are likely to contain intracranial hemorrhage.
method: Retrospective PMCT study of 265 healthy subjects and 33 fatal intracranial hemorrhage cases.
Brain CT slices were extracted, normalized, and analyzed with two diffusion models: AnoDDPM and a classifier-guided diffusion model.
Anomaly scores came from reconstruction error between each slice and its pseudo-healthy reconstruction.
evidence_signal: On image-level evaluation, AnoDDPM achieved AUROC 0.928 and AUPRC 0.794, while the classifier-guided model reached AUROC 0.991 and AUPRC 0.960, each with bootstrap confidence intervals.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective data and limited hemorrhage cases mean external validation is needed before real-world forensic deployment.
paper_title: 2D anomaly detection of fatal cerebral hemorrhage on postmortem CT
